findings.classification: Current source continuation of existing historical candidate, central alias/loader reconciliation still required.
findings.claim: validate_breastplate validates profile, calls Anime.validate with raw wall thickness, and only later checks that thickness is 1–20 mm. Millimeters is a public u16 field; Anime.validate calculates gauge.0 * 2 after its other scalar predicates. With a valid earlier profile, otherwise admitted Anime parameters and gauge at least 32768, that multiplication exceeds u16 before the outer gauge check.
findings.qualification: When overflow checks are enabled, that operation can panic rather than return the designated validation error; with checking disabled, wrapping can produce different downstream checks/error ordering. Build-profile settings, production loader reachability, actual invocation, native failure behavior and accepted meshes are not established. Default profile and default Anime controls in separately read support sources satisfy their earlier stated predicates, but no input, fixture or product was run. Within already admitted 1–20 mm the doubled value fits u16; the risk is the raw pre-admission boundary.

findings.classification: Nonfinding and documented policy question, not a demonstrated rendering defect.
findings.claim: Current screen source iterates nonzero alpha and computes pixel indices using remainder/division by size and normalizes pixel indices by size. Current render source checks size 16–512 and supersampling 1–8 before building exactly size-squared coverage; rasterize_icon passes that coverage and size to occupied_bounds. Thus this source-connected caller has a positive divisor and matching buffer extent. Empty coverage returns None via nonfinite empty bounds.
findings.qualification: The max normalized bound denotes last occupied pixel index divided by size. Whether the public bounds contract instead promises the outer edge of the pixel is unresolved; no UI reader, desired convention, or visual product has been checked. Do not invent a general private helper failure or an off-by-one issue from the formula alone.

lenses.assessment: Catalog identifier remains a raw String with nonempty-trim validation; postcard encoding errors use a typed category, not prose branching. Broader identifier policy and native cause open.
Screen uses native projection coordinates and index/size normalization; armor checks raw millimeter and permille ranges. A named unit is present for Millimeters but does not itself admit gauge range.
Armor wall thickness owner and screen frame/bounds semantics remain distinct design questions, q641/q1791.
Existing Millimeters and Anime construction are reused; neither ensures admitted gauge before multiplication. Existing IconBounds owns native extrema, but expected bound convention is unproven.
Unit-bearing u16 alone cannot represent all breastplate-specific allowed thicknesses; do not impose a global millimeter maximum or make pixel coordinates a physical length.
The raw gauge * 2 appears before the outer bounded check; current candidate q641. Bracer placement uses widened u32 sum, not that same overflow.
Anime lap lift relates to gauge; Bracer coverage plus wrist offset is checked as an aggregate; icon alpha extent and size correlate on the traced caller.
Public raw fields and deserialization can represent out-of-range gauge; validation order matters. No malformed actual input is claimed.
BreastplateConstruction::Anime owns its AnimeDesign payload; solid carries none. No additional enum defect is established in this bounded scope.
Raw bytes hash and validated typed design hashes have distinct entry contracts; a misuse or duplicate authority requires a verified caller.
Original armor body and current file differ; the gate/codec block is textually equal while GENERATOR_VERSION changed. That cannot prove behavior/replay or version-consumer equivalence.
Shown icon render path passes checked size and generated coverage to bounds; shown armor path carries raw wall thickness into inner validation. Further producers and consumers remain unread.
